_transcription: ENGLISH PAGES = the EVEN 0-based indices 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 (printed folios 1, 3, 5 ... 15; folio = idx + 1). idx 0 is the bilingual cover, idx 1 is the Hindi General Instructions, idx 2 is the English General Instructions, and EVERY ODD index 1..13 is a Hindi facing page. The alternating hypothesis HELD EXACTLY and did NOT invert: 7 English content pages against 7 Hindi ones, and the paper's last page (idx 14) is EVEN, so there is no English-only tail page and no blank page. NO ENGLISH OVERFLOW ONTO ANY ODD PAGE - checked, not assumed, by stacking the top 30% of ALL SEVEN odd pages (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13) into one strip and reading it: every one opens in Devanagari from its first line. Two cross-page continuations exist and both are ENGLISH-to-ENGLISH: Q12's passage plus sub-part (i) sit on idx 12 with sub-parts (ii)-(v) on idx 14. The QP PDF has a text layer of ZERO characters (pure scan, `textChars: 0` in the paper index), so every page was read as an image; the marking scheme DOES have a text layer and was read both ways, its Section-C key confirmed by vision on ms/p10.png. STRUCTURE read off the paper's own printed General Instructions on idx 2 and it matches `term2_sci` EXACTLY: 12 questions, all compulsory, THREE sections; Section A Q1-3 @2, Section B Q4-11 @3, Section C Q12 a case-study-based question @5. 6 + 24 + 5 = 35, and the marking scheme's front matter independently says 'A full scale of marks 35 has to be used'. ****FINDING - THIS PAPER DOES CONTAIN MCQs, contrary to both the task brief and lib.ts's own comment on `term2_sci` ('contains NO MCQs at all'). Section C's case study Q12 is FIVE one-mark MCQs, (i) to (v), each with four printed options, and the marking scheme keys them as option letters in a plain table: '12. (i)-a (ii)-b (iii)-c (iv)-b (v)-b', 1 mark each, total 5. Sections A and B are wholly subjective, so the paper is 14 subjective rows and 5 MCQ rows. All five keys were independently re-derived and all five agree with CBSE: (i) i=18 deg < C=20 deg so the ray refracts into the water bending AWAY from the normal = option (a); (ii) area = pi d^2 tan^2 C = pi d^2 / (mu^2 - 1) = (b); (iii) largest critical angle = smallest refractive index = Water = (c); (iv) sin C = 1.0/2.0 so C = 30 deg = (b); (v) sin 30 = 1/mu so mu = 2 and v = c/mu = 1.5e8 m/s = (b).**** INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction 6 prints NO COUNT ('internal choice has been provided in some of the questions'), so the inventory was established by walking the marking scheme, whose text layer holds EXACTLY THREE bare 'OR' lines on their own (ms text lines 189, 723, 1233) and nowhere else. All three were confirmed TWICE more on the paper itself - a printed bold 'OR' on the English page (Q2 on idx 4, Q8 on idx 8, Q11 on idx 10) AND a printed 'अथवा' at the matching place on the Hindi facing page (idx 3, 7, 9). So THREE internal choices: Q2, Q8, Q11. Q1, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q9, Q10 and Q12 carry none; Q5's (i)/(ii)/(iii), Q8(a)'s (i)/(ii), Q9's (a)/(b), Q10's (i)/(ii) and Q11(a)'s (i)/(ii) are sub-parts of one question with no 'OR' between them, not alternatives. Primary branches sum to 2+2+2 + 3*8 + 5 = 35. 19 rows for 12 questions (11 primary + 3 alternatives + 5 case-study sub-parts). CBSE VOIDS: the whole scheme (all 11 rendered pages plus its text layer) was scanned for 'no option', 'full mark', 'award', 'even if', 'hindi', 'english version', 'medium only', 'misprint', 'printing error' and 'full credit'. THERE IS NO MEDIUM-SCOPED AWARD CLAUSE ANYWHERE, so the STOP-and-report case did not arise; there is no keyless void and no dual key. TWO award-regardless notes sit outside Section A - which on this paper is the only place they could sit, Section A being wholly subjective - and both are recorded in `_cbseVoided` on their row: Q6 ('Award this 1 mark even if Q-value is not calculated', a genuine award-regardless clause covering 1 of that question's 3 marks) and Q8(b) ('Give full credit for finding the position by taking n = 3 or n = 4', an accept-either-answer clause of the same shape as a dual key, and notable because the scheme's OWN printed working reaches the non-integer order n = 3.5). Five further notes were read and deliberately NOT recorded as voids because they are ordinary marking latitude that still requires a correct answer: 'Give full credit for other correct explanations' (Q2a), 'Full credit if values on the axis are not mentioned' (Q4 and Q5), 'Give full credit for the differentiation by drawing intensity distribution curves' (Q7) and 'give full credit for the ray diagram of Newtonian telescope' (Q11b). One more, on Q8(a)(ii), is a mark REDUCTION ('Award only 1/2 mark if a student draws ray diagram showing correct position of the image') and is not a void in either direction. DECIMAL POINTS ARE ORDINARY BASELINE FULL STOPS ON THIS PAPER, NOT RAISED DOTS - read off this artifact rather than inherited, and verified at zoom in four independent places: the constants block on idx 2 (6.63, 1.6, 8.854, 9.1, 1.675, 1.673, 6.023, 1.38), the nuclear masses in Q6 (238.05079, 139.90543, 98.90594, 1.008665), the lens and slit data in Q8 (1.5, 0.6, 1.0) and Q9 (331.5), and the Q12 option values on idx 14 (2.0, 1.0, 1.5, 2.2, 2.8). So NOT ONE `{\cdot}` appears in this file. Degree signs are printed as a superscript 'o' throughout and are transcribed as `^\circ`. OUT-OF-SYLLABUS: none. Every topic on this paper (rectifier, photodiode, diode V-I, alpha-scattering, fission Q-value, single-slit diffraction, lenses, photon energy/momentum, prism, EM spectrum, reflecting telescope, total internal reflection) has a live chapter, so no `[Outdated]` chapter was needed and none was invented - which matches what the addendum says was measured for Physics 2022. plan.txt names no reference paper, so every question was transcribed from scratch. FIGURE LOAD: 2 printed figures back 2 rows, both REQUIRED, both on English pages, neither decorative and neither approximated in ASCII - Q10's prism (idx 10) and Q12(i)'s four option drawings (idx 12). Every other 'draw a graph / draw V-I characteristics / with the help of a circuit diagram / with the help of a ray diagram' instruction on this paper is the STUDENT drawing and is deliberately NOT flagged. See each row's `_figure` for what was described and what was withheld.

Sub-part (ii) does not have a single official answer: the marking scheme's own printed working sets (2n+1)600 = (2n+3)480 and reaches n = 3.5 - a NON-INTEGER fringe order, which is physically impossible - then quotes x_n = 4 mm from it, and immediately concedes that n = 3 (3.5 mm) and n = 4 (4.5 mm) both earn full credit. questions._figure: REQUIRED - the stem says only 'as shown in the figure' and names no angle at all, so both the prism's geometry AND the ray's fate at face AC exist only in the drawing. Page idx 10. DESCRIBED (labelling and layout): a triangular prism drawn with apex A at the top and base BC at the bottom; an angle is printed at A and another at B; the symbol for the refractive index is printed inside the triangle; a ray arrives from the lower left and meets face AB at a point labelled M; the ray inside the prism runs from M to a point labelled N on face AC; the angle at M is labelled r1 and the angle at N is labelled r2, both against dotted normals; there is an emergent ray at N. WITHHELD deliberately: the two printed angle VALUES and, above all, the direction the ray takes at face AC relative to that face - that is exactly what sub-part (i) is asking for, since the marking scheme's answer turns on the emergent ray grazing along AC. questions.context: A ray of light travels from a denser to a rarer medium. After refraction, it bends away from the normal. When we keep increasing the angle of incidence, the angle of refraction also increases till the refracted ray grazes along the interface of two media. The angle of incidence for which it happens is called critical angle. If the angle of incidence is increased farther the ray will not emerge and it will be reflected back in the denser medium. This phenomenon is called total internal reflection of light.
